To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a method for finding latent patterns in high-dimensional data by identifying reducible sub-spaces, (2) we show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, (3) we show the applicability of the proposed method in a variety of real-world problems, and (4) we provide a theoretical analysis for the proposed method.

(1) we introduce a novel method for finding local latent subspaces in high-dimensional data and (2) we apply the proposed method on a large-scale real-world dataset to find the most informative subspaces of the data.

we present an approach to find latent patterns in high-dimensional data by identifying feature subspaces that contain the most information about the data and that we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on a number of datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel algorithms for finding latent feature subspaces in high-dimensional data.
identifying the latent patterns that are hidden in the high dimensional data and are not captured by any global transformation.
the problem of finding the reducible substructures in the high-dimensional data, i.e. the substructures that are reducible to a lower dimensional space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to find the reducible sub-spaces in a high dimensional data.
the proposed approach is a novel method for the analysis of high dimensional data.
, while feature selection and dimension reduction are important and useful tools, they are not sufficient for the analysis of high dimensional data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in finding the most informative feature subspace for each sample.
we developed a new method to find latent patterns held by subspaces of the feature space.
we develop a novel framework for identifying latent patterns held by a set of features, called REDUS (reducible subspace).
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by focusing on local patterns, we can discover new and interesting latent structures in the data that are otherwise not captured by existing global methods.
the local latent patterns can be captured via a global feature transformation.
the global patterns are often reducible to local patterns, i.e., a global pattern can be represented in the subspace spanned by a few features.
